# Veteran Concrete

> Veteran owned and operated concrete contractor in Las Vegas, Nevada, serving Las Vegas and Clark County. Owned by US Army veteran Justin Ford. Nevada contractor license #0094181 (C-08 Concrete). Phone (805) 717-5173, email justin@veteranconcretenv.com, office at 1350 E. Flamingo Rd., Las Vegas, NV 89119. Free on-site estimates.

Specialties are stamped concrete, concrete stains and overlays, and decorative concrete textures. The crew also builds driveways, patios and walkways, foundation additions and repairs, retaining and block walls, concrete coatings, and countertops for residential and commercial clients. They often fix substandard concrete by resurfacing it instead of tearing it out.

## Services

- [Stamped Concrete](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/services/stamped-concrete/): Stamped patios, pool decks, walkways, and driveways in flagstone, slate, ashlar, brick, cobblestone, and wood plank patterns. Covers what a complete bid should include, Las Vegas heat and sealing, cost factors, and slip resistance.
- [Concrete Stains & Overlays](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/services/stains-overlays/): Resurfacing cracked, faded, or dated concrete without tear-out using acid stain, water-based stain, stamped overlays, knockdown finishes, microtoppings, and coatings. Explains which slabs qualify for an overlay and which need replacing.
- [Decorative Concrete Textures](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/services/concrete-textures/): Wood grain, stone texture, broom, rock salt, exposed aggregate, and integral colored concrete. Covers grip, heat, and how texturing compares to stamping.

## Common questions

- [Can bad concrete be fixed without replacing it?](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/#faq-title): Often yes, if the slab is structurally sound. Sinking, heaving, or displaced concrete needs replacement.
- [What does stamped concrete cost in Las Vegas?](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/services/stamped-concrete/#faq-title): Depends on size, pattern, number of colors, access, and base prep. Free on-site bids.
- [Does decorative concrete hold up in Las Vegas heat?](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/#faq-title): Yes, with a UV-stable sealer refreshed every few years.
- [Is Veteran Concrete licensed?](https://www.veteranconcretenv.com/#faq-title): Yes, Nevada license #0094181 (C-08 Concrete), verifiable with the Nevada State Contractors Board.
